items.title: Michael Abene interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 11, 2003
items.q: Right now I’m working on a project with Joe Lovano’s wife, Judy Silvano, who is a very good singer.

ctx.x: Right. You’ve done a lot of accompanying of vocalists. Is there a special knack that you have to have for that.

Yeah. Steel fortitude for one. Yeah I’ve sort of gotten away from a lot of it. I think playing for a singer is kind of interesting for a pianist, or an arranger, but especially for a pianist. Because I’ve learned a lot of tunes over the years and in any key. So for pianists, if nothing else, just knowing the repertoire of the great American songs, plus being able ©Fillius Jazz Archive -14-

to play them in a lot of keys. And so for that it was fun. Obviously for some singers I like playing for and dealing with more than others. But I learned, again, I learned a lot. And also I like writing for singers. I haven’t done so much of that in a while. I did a record for Nnenna Freelon about three years ago called “Maiden Voyage” for Concord and we used different small groups. But generally, this wonderful singer, Jennifer Holliday, who did the original “Dream Girls” cast is a wonderful singer. We just did…
